question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(z)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{3}-5{z}^{2} & =-2{z}^{3}+4{z}^{2}+30z \\ 3{z}^{3}-5{z}^{2} & =4{z}^{2}+30z \\ 3{z}^{3}-9{z}^{2} & =30z \\ 3{z}^{3}-9{z}^{2}-30z & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $3z.$ We can factor out the $3z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{3}-9{z}^{2}-30z & =0 \\ 3z({z}^{2}-3z-10) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression ${z}^{2}-3z-10$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3z({z}^{2}-3z-10) & =0 \\ 3z(z-5)(z+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $z=0,$ $z=5,$ and $z=-2.$
